query: What is the equilibrium vapour pressure of solid/liquid MoO3 as a function of temperature between about 600 and 1100 K, and which gas species carry it (monomer MoO3 versus the oligomers Mo3O9, Mo4O12, Mo5O15)? Give the fitted or tabulated expression (log10 P versus 1/T, or sublimation enthalpy and entropy) with units, the temperature range, whether the pressure is the total Mo-bearing vapour or the monomer partial pressure, the numerical value at 1000 K, and the primary experimental sources (for example Berkowitz, Inghram and Chupka 1957; Simnad and Spilners 1956; Gurvich/NIST-JANAF assessments). Cite each number to its source with DOI where available.
answer:
## Equilibrium vapour over MoO₃

**At 1000 K, a published thermochemical fit gives approximately 0.40 Torr (53 Pa) for the *total pressure of MoO₃ oligomers over solid MoO₃*. This is not the partial pressure of gaseous MoO₃ monomer.** The fit is explicitly for the solid and stops at the melting point, approximately 1068 K; it must not be extended unchanged through 1100 K into the liquid region. (smolik2000oxidationvolatilizationand pages 22-25, kim1989synthesispropertiesand pages 19-23)

With temperature **T in K**, Smolik *et al.* give their HSC-derived correlation as

\[
\log_{10}\!\left(\frac{P_{\rm total}}{\mathrm{Torr}}\right)
=\frac{8599.81}{T}-186.495+63.1654\log_{10}T
-0.0078447T-\frac{4\,154\,834}{T^2}.
\]

Their description identifies \(P_{\rm total}\) as the **total pressure of effective polymeric (MoO₃)ₘ vapour over the solid**, not \(p[\mathrm{MoO_3(g)}]\). The report, *Oxidation, Volatilization, and Redistribution of Molybdenum from TZM Alloy in Air* (2000), DOI: [10.2172/752007](https://doi.org/10.2172/752007), derives the correlation from HSC thermochemical data rather than presenting it as a direct measurement of equilibrium pressure. Its stated phase domain is solid MoO₃ up to melting; the report does not establish a separate validity limit at the low-temperature end of the requested 600–1100 K interval. Substitution of 1000 K yields \(\log_{10}(P/\mathrm{Torr})\simeq-0.399\), hence \(P\simeq0.40\) Torr. (smolik2000oxidationvolatilizationand pages 22-25, smolik2000oxidationvolatilizationand pages 35-43)

| Source / basis | Pressure quantity | Expression or tabulation | Temperature range / phase | Value at 1000 K | Scope and caveats |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Smolik et al. (2000), Eq. 6; HSC thermochemical calculation; DOI: [10.2172/752007](https://doi.org/10.2172/752007) | **Total pressure of effective polymeric Mo-bearing vapour**, representing chiefly $(\mathrm{MoO_3})_3$, $(\mathrm{MoO_3})_4$, and $(\mathrm{MoO_3})_5$; not $p(\mathrm{MoO_3})$ monomer | $\log_{10}[P/\mathrm{Torr}]=8599.81/T-186.495+63.1654\log_{10}T-0.0078447T-4154834/T^2$, with $T$ in K (smolik2000oxidationvolatilizationand pages 22-25) | Solid MoO₃ only, stated to apply up to the melting point, approximately 1068 K | $\log_{10}(P/\mathrm{Torr})\approx-0.399$; **$P\approx0.40$ Torr = 53 Pa** | Most usable continuous correlation found for 600–1068 K, but it is an HSC-derived effective-total-pressure fit, not a direct monomer-pressure measurement. No corresponding reliable liquid-phase equation was supplied. |
| Berkowitz, Inghram & Chupka (1957), as reprinted in Fletcher (1966), Table 11; primary DOI: [10.1063/1.1743417](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1743417) | Reported pressure over solid MoO₃ associated with the polymeric vapour; the reprint does not give a monomer partial pressure | $T=883,923,973$ K: $P=2.6,20.1,220.0\times10^{-3}$ mmHg (Torr), respectively (fletcher1966agravimetricand pages 69-73) | 883–973 K tabulation; solid MoO₃ | **Not independently tabulated or validated at 1000 K**; extrapolation is not recommended from only these three reprinted points | Secondary reprint of the 1957 mass-spectrometric results, not an independent experiment. These values differ appreciably from the later HSC fit and should be reported as a separate historical dataset rather than merged with it. |
| Kim (1989), literature summary | **Mo₃O₉ trimer partial pressure**, not total Mo-bearing vapour | $p(\mathrm{Mo_3O_9})=1.64\times10^{-6}$ atm = $1.66\times10^{-1}$ Pa = $1.25\times10^{-3}$ Torr at 861 K (kim1989synthesispropertiesand pages 23-30) | Single point at 861 K; solid-source sublimation | No temperature law, so **no defensible 1000 K value** | Supports trimer predominance but cannot be used as a total-pressure correlation. No reliable monomer-MoO₃ or liquid-MoO₃ pressure equation was identified. |


*Table: Comparison of the usable total-oligomer correlation, the historical Berkowitz pressure tabulation, and a species-specific Mo₃O₉ datum. It distinguishes total Mo-bearing vapour from an individual oligomer partial pressure and identifies unsupported extrapolations.*

### Experimental comparison and vapour species

The pertinent primary mass-spectrometric paper is Berkowitz, Inghram and Chupka, **“Polymeric Gaseous Species in the Sublimation of Molybdenum Trioxide,”** *Journal of Chemical Physics* **26**, 842 (1957), DOI: [10.1063/1.1743417](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1743417). Its full text was not available for verification here. Fletcher’s 1966 reproduction of its pressure measurements over **solid** MoO₃ lists, at **883, 923 and 973 K**, respectively, **2.6, 20.1 and 220.0 × 10⁻³ mmHg**. These are reported as pressures over MoO₃, **not monomer-specific partial pressures**. They disagree substantially with the later HSC-derived fit; the three historical points should not be silently combined with that fit or extrapolated to claim a measured 1000 K pressure. (fletcher1966agravimetricand pages 69-73, fletcher1966agravimetricand pages 277-283, smolik2000oxidationvolatilizationand pages 22-25)

The vapour is **oligomer-rich, principally Mo₃O₉**, with Mo₄O₁₂ and Mo₅O₁₅ also important—not predominantly free MoO₃ molecules. Smolik *et al.* identify the trimer, tetramer and pentamer as the principal species in their temperature region. An independent later study reports a trimer-dominated distribution of sublimed clusters; its **61% trimer, 17% tetramer, 15% pentamer and 7% hexamer** figures come from a separate matrix-isolation measurement and should not be imposed as equilibrium partial-pressure fractions at every temperature. A literature summary quotes **\(p(\mathrm{Mo_3O_9})=1.64\times10^{-6}\) atm at 861 K**: that single **trimer partial-pressure** datum is neither the total pressure nor a fitted monomer-pressure law. (smolik2000oxidationvolatilizationand pages 22-25, doudin2021creatingselfassembledarrays pages 2-3, kim1989synthesispropertiesand pages 23-30)

**Limits of the available evidence.** No verified equilibrium expression for **liquid** MoO₃ between approximately 1068 and 1100 K, or separate temperature-dependent \(p(\mathrm{MoO_3})\), \(p(\mathrm{Mo_3O_9})\), \(p(\mathrm{Mo_4O_{12}})\) and \(p(\mathrm{Mo_5O_{15}})\), was recoverable from the consulted sources. A defensible liquid-region value therefore cannot be supplied by extrapolating the solid fit. Likewise, no numerical Gurvich/NIST–JANAF species-by-species assessment was accessible to independently check it. Simnad and Spilners are cited by Smolik *et al.* as **1955** (*J. Metals* **7**, 1011–1016), for oxidation/volatilization of *molybdenum metal* at **500–770 °C**, not for a direct equilibrium-pressure equation for pure MoO₃; the report gives their apparent activation energies as **53.0 and 89.6 kcal mol⁻¹** below and above **650 °C**. These oxidation-rate energies must not be substituted for an equilibrium sublimation enthalpy. (smolik2000oxidationvolatilizationand pages 35-43, smolik2000oxidationvolatilizationand pages 22-25, fletcher1966agravimetricand pages 69-73)
